sanskrit: taṃ samīkṣya mahāsattvaṃ sattvavān harisattamaḥ vākyam arthavad avyagras tam uvāca daśānanam
english: Beholding that being of immense power, the foremost of monkeys, himself of great courage, composed and unperturbed, spoke words full of meaning to the Ten-faced one.

sanskrit: ahaṃ sugrīvasaṃdeśād iha prāptas tavālayam rākṣasendra harīśas tvāṃ bhrātā kuśalam abravīt
english: "I have come to your abode, O lord of rākṣasas, bearing a message from Sugrīva. The lord of monkeys, your brother, has sent you his greetings.

sanskrit: bhrātuḥ śṛṇu samādeśaṃ sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ dharmārthopahitaṃ vākyam iha cāmutra ca kṣamam
english: Hear the counsel of your brother, the great-souled Sugrīva — words grounded in righteousness and prudence, beneficial both in this world and the next.

sanskrit: rājā daśaratho nāma rathakuñjaravājimān piteva bandhur lokasya sureśvarasamadyutiḥ
english: There was a king named Daśaratha, possessor of chariots, elephants, and horses, a kinsman to the world like a father, equal in splendour to the lord of the gods.

sanskrit: jyeṣṭhas tasya mahābāhuḥ putraḥ priyakaraḥ prabhuḥ pitur nideśān niṣkrāntaḥ praviṣṭo daṇḍakāvanam
english: His eldest son, a mighty-armed lord, beloved and pleasing, departed at his father's command and entered the Daṇḍaka forest.

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā sītayā cāpi bhāryayā rāmo nāma mahātejā dharmyaṃ panthānam āśritaḥ
english: That one of great splendour, named Rāma, accompanied by his brother Lakṣmaṇa and his wife Sītā, followed the path of righteousness.

sanskrit: tasya bhāryā vane naṣṭā sītā patim anuvratā vaidehasya sutā rājño janakasya mahātmanaḥ
english: His wife Sītā, devoted to her husband, the daughter of the great-souled King Janaka of Videha, was lost in the forest.

sanskrit: sa mārgamāṇas tāṃ devīṃ rājaputraḥ sahānujaḥ ṛśyamūkam anuprāptaḥ sugrīveṇa ca saṃgataḥ
english: That prince, searching for the goddess, together with his younger brother, reached Ṛśyamūka and met with Sugrīva.

sanskrit: tasya tena pratijñātaṃ sītāyāḥ parimārgaṇam sugrīvasyāpi rāmeṇa harirājyaṃ niveditam
english: By him was the search for Sītā pledged, and Rāma in turn granted Sugrīva the kingdom of the monkeys.

sanskrit: tatas tena mṛdhe hatvā rājaputreṇa vālinam sugrīvaḥ sthāpito rājye haryṛkṣāṇāṃ gaṇeśvaraḥ
english: Then, having slain Vālin in battle, that prince established Sugrīva as king, lord of the hosts of monkeys and bears.

sanskrit: sa sītāmārgaṇe vyagraḥ sugrīvaḥ satyasaṃgaraḥ harīn saṃpreṣayām āsa diśaḥ sarvā harīśvaraḥ
english: That lord of monkeys, Sugrīva, true to his pledge and intent on the search for Sītā, dispatched monkeys in all directions.

sanskrit: tāṃ harīṇāṃ sahasrāṇi śatāni niyutāni ca dikṣu sarvāsu mārgante adhaś copari cāmbare
english: Thousands, hundreds, and tens of thousands of those monkeys search in all directions, below and above in the sky.

sanskrit: vainateya samāḥ ke cit ke cit tatrānilopamāḥ asaṃgagatayaḥ śīghrā harivīrā mahābalāḥ
english: Some are equal to Garuḍa, son of Vinatā; others are comparable to the wind; those heroic monkeys move without obstruction, swift and of great might.

sanskrit: ahaṃ tu hanumān nāma mārutasyaurasaḥ sutaḥ sītāyās tu kṛte tūrṇaṃ śatayojanam āyatam samudraṃ laṅghayitvaiva tāṃ didṛkṣur ihāgataḥ
english: And I am Hanūmān by name, the own-born son of the Wind-god. For Sītā's sake, crossing in an instant the ocean stretching a hundred yojanas, I came here desiring to find her.

sanskrit: tad bhavān dṛṣṭadharmārthas tapaḥ kṛtaparigrahaḥ paradārān mahāprājña noparoddhuṃ tvam arhasi
english: Therefore you, who have seen the value of righteousness and profit, who have embraced austerities, O greatly wise one — you ought not to obstruct the wife of another.

sanskrit: na hi dharmaviruddheṣu bahv apāyeṣu karmasu mūlaghātiṣu sajjante buddhimanto bhavadvidhāḥ
english: For the wise, such as you, do not engage in acts opposed to righteousness, fraught with many perils, and destructive to the very root.

sanskrit: kaś ca lakṣmaṇamuktānāṃ rāmakopānuvartinām śarāṇām agrataḥ sthātuṃ śakto devāsureṣv api
english: And who is capable of standing before the arrows released by Lakṣmaṇa, following in the wake of Rāma's wrath — even among gods and asuras?

sanskrit: na cāpi triṣu lokeṣu rājan vidyeta kaś cana rāghavasya vyalīkaṃ yaḥ kṛtvā sukham avāpnuyāt
english: Nor in the three worlds, O king, is there anyone who, having wronged Rāghava, might attain happiness.

sanskrit: tat trikālahitaṃ vākyaṃ dharmyam arthānubandhi ca manyasva naradevāya jānakī pratidīyatām
english: Therefore consider this counsel, beneficial in all three times, righteous, and attended by profit: let Jānakī be restored to the lord among men.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭā hīyaṃ mayā devī labdhaṃ yad iha durlabham uttaraṃ karma yac cheṣaṃ nimittaṃ tatra rāghavaḥ
english: For I have seen the goddess — that which was hard to find here has been found. Whatever remaining action follows from this, for that Rāghava is the instrument.

sanskrit: lakṣiteyaṃ mayā sītā tathā śokaparāyaṇā gṛhya yāṃ nābhijānāsi pañcāsyām iva pannagīm
english: I have marked this Sītā, so wholly given over to grief — she whom you hold without recognising her, as one might grasp a five-hooded serpentess.

sanskrit: neyaṃ jarayituṃ śakyā sāsurair amarair api viṣasaṃsṛṣṭam atyarthaṃ bhuktam annam ivaujasā
english: She cannot be overcome even by gods together with asuras, like food mixed with poison consumed to excess is fatal to one's vital energy.

sanskrit: tapaḥsaṃtāpalabdhas te yo 'yaṃ dharmaparigrahaḥ na sa nāśayituṃ nyāyya ātmaprāṇaparigrahaḥ
english: This store of righteousness that you have gained through the heat of austerities — it is not proper to destroy it, together with your own life's refuge.

sanskrit: avadhyatāṃ tapobhir yāṃ bhavān samanupaśyati ātmanaḥ sāsurair devair hetus tatrāpy ayaṃ mahān
english: The invulnerability that you perceive for yourself through your austerities — from gods together with asuras — even that is greatly undermined by this very act.

sanskrit: sugrīvo na hi devo 'yaṃ nāsuro na ca mānuṣaḥ na rākṣaso na gandharvo na yakṣo na ca pannagaḥ
english: For Sugrīva is neither a god, nor an asura, nor a human, nor a rākṣasa, nor a gandharva, nor a yakṣa, nor a serpent.

sanskrit: mānuṣo rāghavo rājan sugrīvaś ca harīśvaraḥ tasmāt prāṇaparitrāṇaṃ kathaṃ rājan kariṣyasi
english: Rāghava is a man, O king, and Sugrīva is the lord of monkeys — how then, O king, will you save your life?

sanskrit: na tu dharmopasaṃhāram adharmaphalasaṃhitam tad eva phalam anveti dharmaś cādharmanāśanaḥ
english: Righteousness does not follow the approach of unrighteousness attended by its fruits; rather, righteousness destroys unrighteousness, and each act bears its own consequence.

sanskrit: prāptaṃ dharmaphalaṃ tāvad bhavatā nātra saṃśayaḥ phalam asyāpy adharmasya kṣipram eva prapatsyase
english: You have already reaped the fruit of your righteous deeds — of that there is no doubt; but you shall swiftly obtain the fruit of this unrighteous act as well.

sanskrit: janasthānavadhaṃ buddhvā buddhvā vālivadhaṃ tathā rāmasugrīvasakhyaṃ ca budhyasva hitam ātmanaḥ
english: Having understood the slaughter at Janasthāna and the slaying of Vālin, and understanding the alliance of Rāma and Sugrīva — recognise what is beneficial for yourself.

sanskrit: kāmaṃ khalv aham apy ekaḥ savājirathakuñjarām laṅkāṃ nāśayituṃ śaktas tasyaiṣa tu viniścayaḥ
english: Indeed I alone am capable of destroying Laṅkā with its horses, chariots, and elephants — but that is his resolve.

sanskrit: rāmeṇa hi pratijñātaṃ haryṛkṣagaṇasaṃnidhau utsādanam amitrāṇāṃ sītā yais tu pradharṣitā
english: For Rāma has pledged, in the presence of the hosts of monkeys and bears, the annihilation of enemies — those by whom Sītā has been violated.

sanskrit: apakurvan hi rāmasya sākṣād api puraṃdaraḥ na sukhaṃ prāpnuyād anyaḥ kiṃ punas tvadvidho janaḥ
english: For even Purandara himself, should he wrong Rāma, would not attain happiness — what then of a person like you?

sanskrit: yāṃ sītety abhijānāsi yeyaṃ tiṣṭhati te vaśe kālarātrīti tāṃ viddhi sarvalaṅkāvināśinīm
english: She whom you know as Sītā, who stands in your power — know her as the night of death, the destroyer of all Laṅkā.

sanskrit: tad alaṃ kālapāśena sītā vigraharūpiṇā svayaṃ skandhāvasaktena kṣamam ātmani cintyatām
english: Enough — Sītā is the very noose of death embodied, clinging of her own accord to your neck; consider well what is fitting for yourself.

sanskrit: sītāyās tejasā dagdhāṃ rāmakopaprapīḍitām dahyamanām imāṃ paśya purīṃ sāṭṭapratolikām
english: Behold this city with its towers and royal highways, scorched by Sītā's blazing power, oppressed by Rāma's wrath, burning even now.

sanskrit: sa sauṣṭhavopetam adīnavādinaḥ kaper niśamyāpratimo 'priyaṃ vacaḥ daśānanaḥ kopavivṛttalocanaḥ samādiśat tasya vadhaṃ mahākapeḥ
english: Having heard the unpleasant yet eloquent words of the monkey who spoke without timidity — words elegant and well-composed — the Ten-faced one, his eyes wide with rage, commanded the slaying of that great monkey.

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā vānarasya mahātmanaḥ ājñāpayad vadhaṃ tasya rāvaṇaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ
english: Having heard those words of the great-souled monkey, Rāvaṇa, overcome with fury, commanded his execution.

sanskrit: vadhe tasya samājñapte rāvaṇena durātmanā niveditavato dautyaṃ nānumene vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: When the wicked-souled Rāvaṇa had commanded his killing, Vibhīṣaṇa — who had duly announced his embassy — did not approve.

sanskrit: taṃ rakṣo'dhipatiṃ kruddhaṃ tac ca kāryam upasthitam viditvā cintayām āsa kāryaṃ kāryavidhau sthitaḥ
english: Knowing the lord of rākṣasas to be enraged and the matter at hand to be critical, he reflected on the right course of action, firm in the conduct of duty.

sanskrit: niścitārthas tataḥ sāmnāpūjya śatrujidagrajam uvāca hitam atyarthaṃ vākyaṃ vākyaviśāradaḥ
english: Having resolved his purpose, and reverently addressing with gentle words his elder brother the conqueror of enemies, that master of speech spoke words of great benefit.

sanskrit: rājan dharmaviruddhaṃ ca lokavṛtteś ca garhitam tava cāsadṛśaṃ vīra kaper asya pramāpaṇam
english: "O king, the killing of this monkey is contrary to righteousness, censured by the conduct of the world, and unworthy of you, O hero.

sanskrit: asaṃśayaṃ śatrur ayaṃ pravṛddhaḥ kṛtaṃ hy anenāpriyam aprameyam na dūtavadhyāṃ pravadanti santo dūtasya dṛṣṭā bahavo hi daṇḍāḥ
english: Without doubt this enemy is grown mighty and has done an immeasurable wrong; yet the righteous do not prescribe death for an envoy — many punishments have been seen for an envoy, but not death.

sanskrit: vairūpyām aṅgeṣu kaśābhighāto mauṇḍyaṃ tathā lakṣmaṇasaṃnipātaḥ etān hi dūte pravadanti daṇḍān vadhas tu dūtasya na naḥ śruto 'pi
english: Disfigurement of the limbs, flogging with a whip, shaving of the head, and the application of Lakṣmaṇa's brand — these are the punishments prescribed for an envoy; but the slaying of an envoy we have not even heard of.

sanskrit: kathaṃ ca dharmārthavinītabuddhiḥ parāvarapratyayaniścitārthaḥ bhavadvidhaḥ kopavaśe hi tiṣṭhet kopaṃ niyacchanti hi sattvavantaḥ
english: And how could one such as you, whose mind is schooled in righteousness and prudence, who is firm in discerning what is high and low, remain in the power of anger? For those of firm character restrain their anger.

sanskrit: na dharmavāde na ca lokavṛtte na śāstrabuddhigrahaṇeṣu vāpi vidyeta kaś cit tava vīratulyas tvaṃ hy uttamaḥ sarvasurāsurāṇām
english: In discourse on righteousness, in the ways of the world, and in the mastery of the intellect through the śāstras, none equals you, O hero — for you are the supreme one among all gods and asuras.

sanskrit: na cāpy asya kaper ghāte kaṃ cit paśyāmy ahaṃ guṇam teṣv ayaṃ pātyatāṃ daṇḍo yair ayaṃ preṣitaḥ kapiḥ
english: Nor do I see any benefit in killing this monkey; let this punishment fall upon those by whom this monkey was sent.

sanskrit: sādhur vā yadi vāsādhur parair eṣa samarpitaḥ bruvan parārthaṃ paravān na dūto vadham arhati
english: Whether righteous or unrighteous, this one has been dispatched by others; speaking on another's behalf, acting under another's authority, an envoy does not deserve death.

sanskrit: api cāsmin hate rājan nānyaṃ paśyāmi khecaram iha yaḥ punar āgacchet paraṃ pāraṃ mahodadhiḥ
english: Moreover, should this one be killed, O king, I see no other sky-traveller who could come again across the great ocean.

sanskrit: tasmān nāsya vadhe yatnaḥ kāryaḥ parapuraṃjaya bhavān sendreṣu deveṣu yatnam āsthātum arhati
english: Therefore no effort should be made to kill him, O conqueror of enemy cities; you ought to direct your effort against the gods with Indra at their head.

sanskrit: asmin vinaṣṭe na hi dūtam anyaṃ paśyāmi yas tau nararājaputrau yuddhāya yuddhapriyadurvinītāv udyojayed dīrghapathāvaruddhau
english: If this one perishes, I see no other envoy who could rouse those two sons of a human king to battle — those two who love battle, who are proud, and who are kept away by the long path.

sanskrit: parākramotsāhamanasvināṃ ca surāsurāṇām api durjayena tvayā manonandana nairṛtānāṃ yuddhāyatir nāśayituṃ na yuktā
english: It is not fitting, O delight of the mind, for you who are difficult to conquer even by the valiant, spirited, and courageous gods and asuras, to destroy the war-enterprise of the rākṣasas.

sanskrit: hitāś ca śūrāś ca samāhitāś ca kuleṣu jātāś ca mahāguṇeṣu manasvinaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ variṣṭhāḥ koṭyagraśaste subhṛtāś ca yodhāḥ
english: Well-disposed, heroic, composed, born into illustrious lineages, high-minded, foremost among weapon-bearers, sharp at the blade's edge, and well-maintained — such are your warriors.

sanskrit: tad ekadeśena balasya tāvat ke cit tavādeśakṛto 'payāntu tau rājaputrau vinigṛhya mūḍhau pareṣu te bhāvayituṃ prabhāvam
english: Let some portion of your forces set out at your command and subdue those two foolish princes, so as to demonstrate your power over your enemies."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā daśagrīvo mahābalaḥ deśakālahitaṃ vākyaṃ bhrātur uttamam abravīt
english: Having heard those words, the mighty Ten-necked one spoke in reply to his brother's excellent counsel, fitting to time and place.

sanskrit: samyag uktaṃ hi bhavatā dūtavadhyā vigarhitā avaśyaṃ tu vadhād anyaḥ kriyatām asya nigrahaḥ
english: "What you have said is correct: the slaying of an envoy is censured. Yet some punishment other than death must certainly be inflicted upon him.

sanskrit: kapīnāṃ kila lāṅgūlam iṣṭaṃ bhavati bhūṣaṇam tad asya dīpyatāṃ śīghraṃ tena dagdhena gacchatu
english: It is said that the tail is dear to monkeys as their ornament — let it be set ablaze at once, and let him depart with it burned.

sanskrit: tataḥ paśyantv imaṃ dīnam aṅgavairūpyakarśitam samitrā jñātayaḥ sarve bāndhavāḥ sasuhṛjjanāḥ
english: Then let his allies, kinsmen, relatives, and all his friends behold him wretched, afflicted with the disfigurement of his limbs."

sanskrit: ājñāpayad rākṣasendraḥ puraṃ sarvaṃ sacatvaram lāṅgūlena pradīptena rakṣobhiḥ pariṇīyatām
english: The lord of rākṣasas commanded: "Let him be led by the rākṣasas through the entire city together with its squares, with his tail set ablaze."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā rākṣasāḥ kopakarkaśāḥ veṣṭante tasya lāṅgūlaṃ jīrṇaiḥ kārpāsikaiḥ paṭaiḥ
english: Having heard that command, the rākṣasas, hardened with rage, began wrapping his tail in old cotton cloths.

sanskrit: saṃveṣṭyamāne lāṅgūle vyavardhata mahākapiḥ śuṣkam indhanam āsādya vaneṣv iva hutāśanaḥ
english: As his tail was being wrapped, the great monkey grew larger, like fire in the forests when it reaches dry fuel.

sanskrit: tailena pariṣicyātha te 'gniṃ tatrāvapātayan
english: Then, having drenched it with oil, they set fire to it.

sanskrit: lāṅgūlena pradīptena rākṣasāṃs tān apātayat roṣāmarṣaparītātmā bālasūryasamānanaḥ
english: With his tail ablaze, his spirit filled with fury and indignation, his face like the rising sun, he flung those rākṣasas down.

sanskrit: sa bhūyaḥ saṃgataiḥ krūrai rākasair harisattamaḥ nibaddhaḥ kṛtavān vīras tatkālasadṛśīṃ matim
english: Bound again by the cruel rākṣasas who gathered around him, that foremost of monkeys, that hero, formed a resolve suited to the moment.

sanskrit: kāmaṃ khalu na me śaktā nibadhasyāpi rākṣasāḥ chittvā pāśān samutpatya hanyām aham imān punaḥ
english: "Indeed, these rākṣasas are not capable of binding me; even now, bound as I am, I could cut the bonds, leap up, and slay them.

sanskrit: sarveṣām eva paryāpto rākṣasānām ahaṃ yudhi kiṃ tu rāmasya prītyarthaṃ viṣahiṣye 'ham īdṛśam
english: I am fully capable of defeating all rākṣasas in battle; yet for Rāma's pleasure I shall endure this circumstance."

sanskrit: laṅkā carayitavyā me punar eva bhaved iti rātrau na hi sudṛṣṭā me durgakarmavidhānataḥ avaśyam eva draṣṭavyā mayā laṅkā niśākṣaye
english: "It would be well if I were to survey Laṅkā once more — for at night I did not see it clearly enough in terms of its fortifications and their arrangement; I must certainly examine Laṅkā before night is spent."

sanskrit: kāmaṃ bandhaiś ca me bhūyaḥ pucchasyoddīpanena ca pīḍāṃ kurvantu rakṣāṃsi na me 'sti manasaḥ śramaḥ
english: "Let the rākṣasas torment me further with bonds and the burning of my tail — my mind feels no weariness."

sanskrit: tatas te saṃvṛtākāraṃ sattvavantaṃ mahākapim parigṛhya yayur hṛṣṭā rākṣasāḥ kapikuñjaram
english: Then those rākṣasas, joyful, seized that mighty monkey who concealed his feelings — that elephant among monkeys, of great courage — and led him away.

sanskrit: śaṅkhabherīninādais tair ghoṣayantaḥ svakarmabhiḥ rākṣasāḥ krūrakarmāṇaś cārayanti sma tāṃ purīm
english: Those rākṣasas of cruel deeds, proclaiming their own acts with the sounds of conch-shells and kettledrums, led him through the city.

sanskrit: hanumāṃś cārayām āsa rākṣasānāṃ mahāpurīm athāpaśyad vimānāni vicitrāṇi mahākapiḥ
english: Hanūmān was led through the great city of the rākṣasas, and the great monkey observed its wonderful aerial palaces.

sanskrit: saṃvṛtān bhūmibhāgāṃś ca suvibhaktāṃś ca catvarān rathyāś ca gṛhasaṃbādhāḥ kapiḥ śṛṅgāṭakāni ca
english: The monkey observed the enclosed ground areas, the well-laid-out squares, the streets dense with houses, and the crossroads.

sanskrit: catvareṣu catuṣkeṣu rājamārge tathaiva ca ghoṣayanti kapiṃ sarve cārīka iti rākṣasāḥ
english: In the public squares, at the crossroads, and along the royal highway, all the rākṣasas proclaimed the monkey a spy.

sanskrit: dīpyamāne tatas tasya lāṅgūlāgre hanūmataḥ rākṣasyas tā virūpākṣyaḥ śaṃsur devyās tad apriyam
english: Then, as the tip of Hanūmān's tail was blazing, those rākṣasa women of distorted eyes reported that unpleasant news to the goddess.

sanskrit: yas tvayā kṛtasaṃvādaḥ sīte tāmramukhaḥ kapiḥ lāṅgūlena pradīptena sa eṣa pariṇīyate
english: "That copper-faced monkey with whom you conversed, O Sītā — this very one is being led about with his tail set on fire."

sanskrit: śrutvā tad vacanaṃ krūram ātmāpaharaṇopamam vaidehī śokasaṃtaptā hutāśanam upāgamat
english: Hearing those cruel words, like a seizure of her own self, Vaidehī, burning with grief, approached the fire-god.

sanskrit: maṅgalābhimukhī tasya sā tadāsīn mahākapeḥ upatasthe viśālākṣī prayatā havyavāhanam
english: With wide eyes, pure and auspiciously disposed, she turned toward the great monkey's well-being and propitiated the bearer of oblations.

sanskrit: yady asti patiśuśrūṣā yady asti caritaṃ tapaḥ yadi cāsty ekapatnītvaṃ śīto bhava hanūmataḥ
english: "If there is service rendered to my husband, if there is austerity performed, if there is fidelity to one husband — be cool for Hanūmān."

sanskrit: yadi kaś cid anukrośas tasya mayy asti dhīmataḥ yadi vā bhāgyaśeṣaṃ me śīto bhava hanūmataḥ
english: "If that wise one has any compassion for me, if there remains any residue of my fortune — be cool for Hanūmān."

sanskrit: yadi māṃ vṛttasaṃpannāṃ tatsamāgamalālasām sa vijānāti dharmātmā śīto bhava hanūmataḥ
english: "If that righteous-souled one knows me to be of virtuous conduct and longing for union with him — be cool for Hanūmān."

sanskrit: yadi māṃ tārayaty āryaḥ sugrīvaḥ satyasaṃgaraḥ asmād duḥkhān mahābāhuḥ śīto bhava hanūmataḥ
english: "If the noble, long-armed Sugrīva, true to his pledge, will rescue me from this suffering — be cool for Hanūmān."

sanskrit: tatas tīkṣṇārcir avyagraḥ pradakṣiṇaśikho 'nalaḥ jajvāla mṛgaśāvākṣyāḥ śaṃsann iva śivaṃ kapeḥ
english: Then the fire, with its sharp flames, undisturbed, with its crest turning rightward, blazed — as though proclaiming auspiciousness for the monkey to the doe-eyed one.

sanskrit: dahyamāne ca lāṅgūle cintayām āsa vānaraḥ pradīpto 'gnir ayaṃ kasmān na māṃ dahati sarvataḥ
english: And as his tail burned, the monkey reflected: "This fire is fully kindled — why does it not burn me everywhere?"

sanskrit: dṛśyate ca mahājvālaḥ karoti ca na me rujam śiśirasyeva saṃpāto lāṅgūlāgre pratiṣṭhitaḥ
english: "It is seen to have great flames, yet it causes me no pain; it is stationed at the tip of my tail like a touch of cool snow."

sanskrit: atha vā tad idaṃ vyaktaṃ yad dṛṣṭaṃ plavatā mayā rāmaprabhāvād āścaryaṃ parvataḥ saritāṃ patau
english: "Or rather, this is clearly the same wonder that I witnessed as I flew — through Rāma's power — when Mainākā appeared in the ocean, lord of rivers."

sanskrit: yadi tāvat samudrasya mainākasya ca dhīmatha rāmārthaṃ saṃbhramas tādṛk kim agnir na kariṣyati
english: "If the ocean and the wise Mainākā showed such solicitude for Rāma's purpose, why would fire not do the same?"

sanskrit: sītāyāś cānṛśaṃsyena tejasā rāghavasya ca pituś ca mama sakhyena na māṃ dahati pāvakaḥ
english: "By reason of Sītā's compassion, by the power of Rāghava, and by my father's friendship with him — Pāvaka does not burn me."

sanskrit: bhūyaḥ sa cintayām āsa muhūrtaṃ kapikuñjaraḥ utpapātātha vegena nanāda ca mahākapiḥ
english: Again that elephant among monkeys reflected for a moment, then leaped up with great speed, and the great monkey roared.

sanskrit: puradvāraṃ tataḥ śrīmāñ śailaśṛṅgam ivonnatam vibhaktarakṣaḥsaṃbādham āsasādānilātmajaḥ
english: Then the glorious son of the Wind-god reached the city gate, lofty as a mountain peak, thronged with rākṣasa guards stationed at their posts.

sanskrit: sa bhūtvā śailasaṃkāśaḥ kṣaṇena punar ātmavān hrasvatāṃ paramāṃ prāpto bandhanāny avaśātayat
english: Becoming mountain-like in an instant, then again self-composed and reduced to the smallest size, he shook off his bonds.

sanskrit: vimuktaś cābhavac chrīmān punaḥ parvatasaṃnibhaḥ vīkṣamāṇaś ca dadṛśe parighaṃ toraṇāśritam
english: And freed, the glorious one again became like a mountain; looking about, he spied an iron bar resting against the gatehouse arch.

sanskrit: sa taṃ gṛhya mahābāhuḥ kālāyasapariṣkṛtam rakṣiṇas tān punaḥ sarvān sūdayām āsa mārutiḥ
english: Seizing it, long-armed Māruti — that bar fitted with black iron — slaughtered all those guards once more.

sanskrit: sa tān nihatvā raṇacaṇḍavikramaḥ samīkṣamāṇaḥ punar eva laṅkām pradīptalāṅgūlakṛtārcimālī prakāśatāditya ivāṃśumālī
english: Having slain them, he of fierce prowess in battle, surveying Laṅkā once more, shone resplendent — his tail ablaze making a garland of flames — like the sun with its garland of rays.
